problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{-{n}^{3}+10}{3{n}^{2}-n}$ for $n\ge 1?$
worked_solution:
The dominant term in the denominator is $3{n}^{2},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{-{n}^{3}+10}{3{n}^{2}-n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(-\frac{{n}^{3}}{{n}^{2}}+\frac{10}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{n}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(-n+\frac{10}{{n}^{2}})}{(3-\frac{1}{n})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{-n+0}{3-0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(-\frac{n}{3}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.
